title: When Morning Begins
logline: In one small town, 'morning' begins at a different hour for the baker, the fisher, the drummer and the farmer.

object.note: Object 1 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The dawn reached at the summit carries into the next film's question: when does 'morning' actually begin, and who decides it?

thread_out.thread: The early sounds that mark the start of a day lead into a monastic school where the day begins with recitation: names learned for what happens inside.

lesson.in_simple_terms: 'Morning' is not a thing you can point to. It is a shared agreement, based on the movement of the sun, that people use to organise their lives, so the baker, the fisher, the drummer and the farmer can each have a morning that starts at a different hour.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: 'උදෑසන' යනු ඇඟිල්ල දිගු කර පෙන්විය හැකි දෙයක් නොව, හිරුගේ ගමන පදනම් කරගෙන මිනිසුන් තම ජීවිත සකසා ගැනීමට එකඟ වූ සම්මුතියකි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma texts list time and direction among the meaning-concepts (attha-paññatti): things the mind takes up that are not ultimately present as things. One text explains that the concepts of direction and time arise with the movement of the sun and moon as their basis, and another gives dawn, evening and night as examples of time-concepts. Such concepts belong to conventional, everyday speech (sammuti), which the texts treat as a legitimate way of speaking and teaching, not as an error.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film follows one night turning into day through people whose work decides when their morning starts: ovens lit before dawn, boats coming in, temple drums, a farmer in the first light. The viewer hears several 'mornings' arrive at different hours while the light itself changes slowly and evenly, and notices that the word is placed on the light by each person's life.

key_terms.en: direction and time, based on the movement of sun and moon
meaning-concept: the thing the mind takes up

lesson.caution: This does not mean time is fake or that anyone's morning is wrong; 'morning' is a useful shared name, not a separate thing standing apart from the sun, the light and the people.
lesson.builds_on: Where the first film showed many names for one mountain, this film shows one name, 'morning', that everyone relies on but no one can point to.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
